newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia responds to rebel threat over prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Colombia responds to rebel threat over prisoners.

text.p: With the release of 60 Colombian soldiers at stake, President Ernesto Samper warned his army on Monday that it was forbidden to operate undercover in a zone demilitarized as part of a deal with their guerrilla captors.

His comments come less than 24 hours after leftist rebels said undercover military operations in the jungles of Caqueta province could hamper the release of the troops, held for more than nine months.

Samper ordered government troops to pull out of a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) area of Caqueta to allow Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels to release the 60 soldiers, captured in an attack in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30.

Late Sunday FARC commanders issued a communique saying some of the 5,000 troops withdrawn from the neutral zone returned, posing as street vendors. Gen. Agustin Ardila, commander of the army's Fourth Division, rejected the claim.

By midday Monday, government negotiators and Catholic Church representatives were still waiting to meet with guerrilla leaders in Cartagena del Chaira, the main town in the demilitarized zone. Two days were set aside for the talks under the deal, after which the guerrillas would have two weeks to hand over the captives.
